description: AITHON is my solo project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It aims to make NASA microgravity combustion research easier to explore by organizing experimental data and publications into searchable, comparable, source-linked evidence. The platform will help users investigate experimental conditions, trace findings to original NASA sources, and identify evidence gaps without presenting unsupported conclusions as facts.

details:
AITHON is an interactive scientific research and simulation platform designed to explore liquid fuel droplet physics under microgravity-relevant conditions.

At its core is Model A, an interactive numerical simulator that models transient heat conduction inside a spherical liquid fuel droplet with a moving boundary. It uses the Landau coordinate transformation and a conservative Finite Volume Method (FVM) to calculate time-dependent temperature distributions, surface heat flux and energy balance.

AITHON transforms these numerical results into an interactive 3D scientific visualization using Babylon.js. The droplet's geometry, concentric thermal layers, temperature gradients and radius evolution are driven directly by actual numerical solver snapshots. A synchronized 2D temperature profile, interactive timeline and scientific telemetry help users inspect the simulation.

The platform also integrates NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) for experimental investigation and dataset discovery, and NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) for scientific literature research. Its computational ecosystem includes Python, TypeScript, Cantera, GRI-Mech 3.0 and CoolProp.

AITHON is designed to make complex scientific computing more interactive, accessible and transparent. Model A is explicitly identified as an illustrative numerical prototype, not NASA flight-measurement data. Full coupled combustion execution remains subject to established scientific governance restrictions.
